sector: Rural Asset Management / Financial Services (NZ Agri)
overview: Allied Farmers is the surviving remnant of a 2009-era NZ finance-company collapse (it absorbed Hanover Finance and United Finance's loan books) that has spent 15+ years rebuilding into a small-cap rural investment and asset-management company with a large ($172m) unrecognised tax loss pool. Following the 1 December 2025 sale of its 67.8%-owned livestock agency NZ Farmers Livestock (NZFL) to Rural Livestock Limited, Allied is now a pure-play rural asset manager: its core asset is 100% ownership of New Zealand Rural Land Management (NZRLM), the external manager of NZX-listed farmland REIT New Zealand Rural Land Company (NZL), alongside a parent-level investment portfolio (a ~2.75% NZL shareholding, a $10.5m Waikato investment property, and a $3m secured farm loan). It operates entirely within New Zealand and is listed on the NZX Main Board (ALF).

business_model.summary: Allied now earns recurring, asset-based management, transaction and performance fees from NZRLM's contract to manage NZL's farmland portfolio, supplemented by parent-level investment income (rent, interest, dividends) and the run-off of a large legacy tax-loss pool that shelters future profits from tax. The FY2025-vintage livestock agency/finance business (NZFL) that historically drove ~85% of consolidated revenue has been divested and is now shown as a discontinued operation; H1 FY2026 is the first period reported on a pure continuing-operations (asset management) basis.

revenue_streams.name: NZ Farmers Livestock (livestock agency, veal export, finance) - DIVESTED Dec-2025

business_model.customer_type: B2B/institutional - single major counterparty (NZL, an NZX-listed REIT) for management fees; farm-loan borrower and property tenant relationships at parent level

main_competitors: Colliers/Bayleys rural real estate & farm management teams
Rural Livestock Limited (livestock agency, now owns former NZFL business)
Direct farmland ownership/syndicates as an alternative to NZL
competitive_position.market_position: Niche, single-mandate external manager of one NZX-listed farmland vehicle (NZL); very small market capitalisation (micro-cap) with limited scale versus diversified rural services players

moat_factors.description: NZRLM holds the management contract for NZL, a listed structure with switching costs and governance friction, but the contract itself is not perpetual/guaranteed and NZL could in theory internalise management or replace the manager
Managing Director Richard Milsom co-founded NZRLM/NZL and holds ~15.8% of Allied; WAF Limited (a friendly ~20% holder) provides stable, aligned ownership reducing takeover/activist risk

A substantial legacy tax-loss pool shelters future profits from tax, provided shareholder continuity thresholds are maintained - a real economic asset unusual for a company this size, and a stated capital-allocation driver (Allied prioritises growth investments that can use the losses over dividends)

moat_factors.factor: Niche expertise in NZ farmland/agri asset management
moat_factors.description: Specialist knowledge of NZ pastoral, horticultural and forestry land valuation and management built over years running NZL's ~17,000ha portfolio

weaknesses: Single-client revenue concentration - NZRLM's fee income depends almost entirely on the size, performance and continued existence of one external entity, NZL
Very small scale and float - illiquid micro-cap stock with concentrated register (WAF 19.99%, Rem Trustee 12.45%, Milsom 15.8%) limiting institutional interest
No pricing power over management fee terms, which are set by a negotiated management agreement with NZL and can be reviewed/renegotiated (evidenced by NZL's Feb-2026 KPMG capital review)
History of destroyed shareholder capital during the 2009-2012 finance-company collapse continues to weigh on market perception/valuation
Post-NZFL-sale earnings base is small and volatile, with H1 FY2026 continuing operations posting a pre-tax loss

growth_drivers: Growth in NZL's farmland AUM (acquisitions, portfolio revaluation) directly grows NZRLM's base and performance fees

NZL's Feb-2026 'YieldPlusGrowth' capital management framework (post-KPMG review) targets disciplined, accretive growth and reinstated dividends, which could expand NZL's capital base and Allied's fee pool over time
Redeployment of NZFL sale proceeds (~$5.8m received, ~$2.4m still owed) plus existing cash (~$10.8m at Dec-2025) into new rural investments that can utilise the $172m tax-loss pool
Full realisation of continuing involvement in NZFL's residual loan book (expected recovery by May 2026) releasing further cash
Simplified, focused strategy as a pure asset manager/investor may re-rate the stock versus its prior diversified/lower-margin livestock trading business
Potential for NZRLM to win additional mandates or expand services beyond NZL over time

business.description: Virtually all continuing-operations fee income comes from the NZRLM/NZL management agreement; loss, renegotiation, or underperformance of NZL would materially impair Allied's earnings

business.risk: Small, volatile earnings base post-NZFL divestment
business.description: H1 FY2026 continuing operations posted a pre-tax loss of $0.517m; the company is still bedding down its new operating model and cost base
Strategy depends on management successfully redeploying sale proceeds and cash into new rural investments/loans that generate adequate risk-adjusted returns

financial.risk: Illiquidity of NZL shares and investment property
financial.description: Allied holds ~2.75% of NZL and a $10.5m investment property (via an SPV, MC Redlands-financed) - both are relatively illiquid, fair-value-marked assets

The Waikato property SPV loan (MC Redlands Pty Ltd, $10.5m fair-valued financial liability) is complex and its fair value has already moved materially ($9.568m initial recognition to $10.496m by Jun-2025)

financial.risk: Continuing involvement obligation on NZFL loan book
financial.description: Allied retains ~67.77% economic exposure to NZFL's transferred loan book until fully recovered (expected by May 2026), including exposure to any shortfall

regulatory.risk: Shareholder continuity rules threaten tax loss utilisation
regulatory.description: The $172.4m unrecognised tax loss pool can only be used if NZ shareholder continuity thresholds continue to be met; Allied has already amended its constitution and obtained NZX/NZ RegCo waivers (2024) to restrict share transfers and protect continuity

regulatory.risk: NZX Major Transaction / FMC Act compliance
regulatory.description: Significant transactions (e.g., the NZFL sale) require shareholder approval as Major Transactions under NZX Listing Rule 5.1.1(a), creating execution/timing risk for future portfolio moves

macro.risk: NZ farmland values and agri-commodity cycle
macro.description: NZRLM fee income (especially performance fees) is tied to NZL's net asset value, which moves with NZ farmland valuations, dairy/livestock prices, and farmer confidence
Parent-level and subsidiary borrowings (Heartland Bank facility at BKBM+4%, MC Redlands loan) are sensitive to NZ interest rates; investment property values are also rate-sensitive

macro.risk: US tariffs / geopolitical impact on NZ agri exports
macro.description: Indirect exposure via NZL's farm tenants and broader NZ agri sentiment, though direct livestock/export exposure has been removed with the NZFL sale

macro_factors.industry_outlook: NZ farmland values and the listed rural-land/asset-management niche remain small but are supported by a cyclical upswing in NZ agri commodity prices (strong 2024/25 dairy and livestock pricing) and renewed institutional interest in farmland as an asset class (evidenced by NZL's capital review and move to a dividend-paying 'yield plus growth' model in Feb-2026)
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - NZRLM fee income (particularly performance fees) is linked to NZL's NAV and transaction activity, which correlates with the NZ dairy/agri cycle and land values; parent investment income is comparatively stable
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - direct impact on Allied's own borrowings (Heartland facility, MC Redlands property loan) and on NZL's cost of capital, land valuations and appetite for further acquisitions
key_input_costs: NZ farmland valuations (drives performance fees, not a direct input cost)

recent_developments.event: Allied Farmers announced a conditional agreement to sell 100% of NZ Farmers Livestock Limited (NZFL) to Rural Livestock Limited for an enterprise value of $10.988m
Shareholders approved the NZFL sale as a Major Transaction at the Annual Meeting

Sale of NZFL to Rural Livestock Limited completed; NZFL deconsolidated. Allied received $5.814m of its ~67.77% share of proceeds in H1 FY2026, with ~$2.4m still due; Allied retains continuing involvement/exposure in NZFL's residual loan book (expected to be recovered by May 2026), recognising a $1.932m continuing involvement obligation and $2.745m of related receivables at 31 Dec 2025

H1 FY2026 (six months to 31 Dec 2025) results: consolidated profit after tax of $3.542m (+44.8% YoY), driven by the NZFL sale gain and a $2.740m income tax benefit; continuing operations (post-NZFL, i.e. the ongoing asset-management business) posted a pre-tax LOSS of $0.517m due to NZFL sale transaction costs and higher NZRLM operating/transaction costs; NTA per share rose to $0.70 (from $0.50/$0.54); no interim dividend declared

NZL (the entity NZRLM manages) completed an independent KPMG capital review, announcing a new 'YieldPlusGrowth' capital management framework prioritising sustainable cash yield and disciplined, accretive growth; NZL resumed paying shareholder dividends during FY25/26

FY2025 annual report: audited NPAT of $3.841m (FY24: $6.919m, which included a one-off $4.2m Frankton saleyards gain); FY25 profit after tax attributable to Allied shareholders of $2.871m, EPS 9.97cps; NZFL delivered a much-improved result on a buoyant livestock market

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 results (six months to 31 December 2025), released February 2026

items.target: No dividends; retain and redeploy earnings
items.notes: Management reiterated its long-standing no-dividend policy, prioritising redeployment of earnings/proceeds into growth investments that can utilise the $172.4m tax-loss pool
Allied expects NZFL's transferred loan book to be fully repaid by May 2026, releasing Allied from its continuing involvement obligation
Balance of Allied's ~67.77% share of the $10.988m NZFL enterprise value sale proceeds, following $5.814m already received in H1

items.target: NZRLM to achieve NPBT 10% higher than FY25 NPAT (25% weight); strategy/transaction/leadership targets (75% weight)
items.notes: Reflects the shift to a pure NZRLM/asset-management focus following the NZFL divestment; implies management expects NZRLM NPBT growth of at least 10% in FY26

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Shelley Ruha and MD Richard Milsom framed the NZFL sale as completing Allied's transformation into a focused rural asset manager and investor, deploying capital and tax losses into opportunities managed via its governance structures and NZRLM asset-management expertise. Management noted the Board 'strongly believes retaining and redeploying earnings into investment opportunities that offer sustainable earnings is in shareholders' best interests,' and highlighted continued positive momentum in NZ farm gate conditions into FY26 (albeit with softening in veal/skin pricing prior to the NZFL sale, and uncertainty from US tariffs on NZ agri exports).

bull_case: Simplified, higher-margin business model post-NZFL sale: Allied is now a focused rural asset manager (NZRLM) plus an investment portfolio, removing the lower-margin, working-capital-intensive livestock trading business
Enormous unrecognised tax-loss asset ($172.4m) provides years of tax-free compounding for future earnings, provided shareholder continuity is preserved - a structural advantage most micro-caps lack
NZL's Feb-2026 KPMG-driven 'YieldPlusGrowth' framework and resumed dividends could grow NZL's AUM and investor appeal, directly benefiting NZRLM's recurring and performance-fee income
Strong NZ dairy/agri pricing cycle into FY26 supports farmland valuations (performance fees) and the broader rural investment opportunity set Allied is redeploying capital into

Aligned, concentrated insider/friendly ownership (Milsom 15.8%, WAF 19.99%) reduces takeover overhang and points to management incentives tied to long-term NPAT growth (LTIP tied to 3-year average Group NPAT)
bear_case: Single-mandate concentration risk: nearly all continuing-operations revenue now depends on one management contract with NZL; any renegotiation, internalisation, or NZL underperformance would be highly damaging

Post-divestment earnings base is small and currently loss-making at the operating level (H1 FY26 continuing operations pre-tax loss of $0.517m), so near-term profitability depends on successful capital redeployment that has not yet been proven
Illiquid micro-cap with a small, concentrated share register and thin trading volumes, likely commanding a persistent valuation discount and limiting institutional/index interest
No dividends and reliance on management's capital-allocation judgement to redeploy sale proceeds and cash into new rural investments - execution risk with no committed pipeline disclosed

Complex related structures (NZL-linked management fees paid partly in NZL shares/performance fees, fair-valued SPV property financing, continuing involvement in the divested NZFL loan book) add valuation and disclosure complexity for outside investors
Legacy reputational overhang from the 2009-2012 Hanover/United Finance collapse continues to be part of the company's history and market narrative
